place_name: The Edgewater Hotel B&B Style Inn (Winter Garden)
address: 99 W Plant St, Winter Garden, FL 34787
review:
Happened across this place last year and liked it so much I planned a trip back with my sisters.  We stayed in the king 2-br suite, which was a king, full, and twin bed with a jack & jill style bathroom between the two rooms, and a sink in each.  Only complaint about the room (same as the last stay) is you can really only use hot water to shower because if you have any cold water on, it will intermittently hit you with an icy blast.  But it's a very old building and not a big enough deal to get worked up about.

I was more than a little apprehensive about the religious materials everywhere, but to each their own, the staff are tremendous.  The place is extremely charming, a 2-star rating is underselling it by a lot.  The first time here we actually abandoned our room in a 4-star Orlando resort and stayed here instead.  It's not new/pristine luxury, but it's a well cared-for historic hotel run by people that are personally invested in it.

The included breakfast was phenomenal, made-to-order from a full menu and everything I had was perfect.  The staff were, to a person, extremely helpful and kind.  Hannah especially deserves special mention for dealing with our headache of a moving target check-in date & time.  I dealt with Alicia over email and she helped adjust our reservation and the entire experience was 10x better and easier than dealing with a corporate hotel.

Overall the hotel is a fantastic value, the people are tremendous, the location is perfect (park your car at check-in and you won't need it again until you leave), and it's the reason Winter Garden (and the Edgewater specifically) is going to be my go-to weekend trip spot as long as it remains.
response_of_owner: We deeply appreciate your thorough review! We're especially happy to hear our staff exceeded expectations and that the amenities and historic charm were to your liking. We continue to try and improve upon the plumbing where possible due to the historic nature of the building's construction. Thank you again for your great review and hope to see you again!

review: Cannot rate low enough.  They dropped off a massive window to be installed three weeks prior to our scheduled install date without calling ahead, and told us that we had to store it ourselves at our house.  On the day of our scheduled install the workers left after an hour of work (install was supposed to be a total of two hours) and didn't come back until 3.5 hours later and only because I called the supervisor after 2.5 hours had passed and no one returned.  The supervisor himself had no idea where they were or why they hadn't returned, except to tell me he was sure they had come back to the workshop in the last 2.5 hours to get the necessary materials to finish the install.  When a single worker returned after 3.5 hours he did not have the material to finish the job and it was the end of the work day, so after assessing what was needed they said they would return first thing the next morning between 7:45am and 8am.  They were over an hour late the next morning and left a mess that the supervisor only sent someone out to clean up a full week later and only after I called after waiting a week and asked him to send people that day; his suggested solution was to wait through another weekend after already waiting an entire week, and they would send someone "first thing Monday morning".  Overall, a two hour window install took 24 hours total (from 10am on the first day to 10am on the following day) and required myself or my wife to be there at home during Newman Window's "working hours" for 7 hours the first day and 3 hours on the second day.  I addressed all this to them in person at their offices, at which time they assured me they would review our invoice and get back with an adjusted one.  After waiting a week for a call back, I contacted them again and insisted they clean up the mess they left, which as detailed above they were slow to do.  After another week, they called my wife and had her pay the original invoice in full.  When I contacted them after they had solicitated and received full payment, they were sure to make it clear that their timelines and level or service were acceptable, and that I needed to be understanding because "we're in the middle of a pandemic."

That being said, we want to clarify that in this case the window delivery came directly from the manufacturer, and they are responsible for communicating the delivery logistics. Also there seems to be a miscommunication about the original install. Our crew showed up early after approving it with Kim, to get a jump on your install before their other job. I hope that clears up why they had to leave and return later. Our Director of Operations was able to send a supervisor to clean up the glass you mentioned but knowing we did not have to break any windows during your installation our installers found that it was a random bottle and cleaned it up regardless. review:
It’s a little unthinkable that, for the price of the hotel, the series of unfortunate events that unfolded is allowed.

Upon checkin we were asked if we wanted a dehumidifier for the hotel room for a $30 upcharge. I’ve never been asked this question in my life; I’m from the surrounding area and assumed it must be for out-of-town folks that aren’t used to humidity.

It was not.

The rooms (yes, plural, we were in three different ones) were muggy. Mold is growing actively on the curtains. The air was nothing short of fetid and made our throats and chest gunk up. The sheets and carpet were damp with humidity.

In the evening of the second night our AC broke, in fact the whole hotel’s broke down. In July. In Florida. The hotel staff tried to be reassuring that maintenance was working diligently to restore cooling…. But it was not restored until the following morning when we were checking out. That’s a sweaty night on top of the already swampy atmosphere… and I’m not Shrek.

The hotel staff were quick to respond and tried to be helpful as they could, but I think there’s systemic issues here that are beyond their ability to provide support.

The surrounding area feels a little like a ghost town. What were obviously meant to be upscale shops and restaurants are now things like a karate school and an IT school.

This area may have once been nice… but its majesty is currently that of a bloated whale carcass, dying in isolation in the Florida heat.

The pool was alright.

review:
Overall we were pretty disappointed, mainly because the hotel charged an additional 16% per night on top of what we had paid via Priceline - and before you reply to this review trying to tell me that Priceline did mention this fee on their website - they did not. They did mentioned what they call a "resort fees" which was due upon arrival and we were prepared to pay - they did not mention an additional 16% on top of those fees. Your own staff has a sign on their reception explaining this as soon as guest check in, which, pretty much by the hotel's admission and probably because they had to deal with angry customers who booked through a 3rd party before, shows that there is an extra fee on top off regular fees incurred when booking with third party services.

If you want to stop collecting 2 star reviews, I suggest you sort out this discrepancy with Priceline yourself instead of blaming the customers. It's really up to you, though.

I've attached a photo of the aforementioned sign on their reception desk for your consideration.

That all aside, this hotel is lacking in many ways when you consider the price we paid (which was about 1,000 USD for one king room for 4 nights):

- no turn over service
- single roll of toilet paper
- no microwave/coffee machine in room
- no bar / bit of a dead lobby in general
- no free parking (only 70USD/night valet parking)
- shitty (but free) coffee

The only saving grace were the gym, decent room & bed sizes and, of course, the location. Location alone does not make for a great experience, though, especially for the prices they ask for and put a damper on our vacation to Chicago.

There is a reason this hotel has currently 2.6 stars on average over 600+ reviews.
If you're looking for a downtown stay, do yourself a favor and look for a hotel in the area that is worth the money.
response_of_owner: Juls:  Had you booked directly through our Hotel you would see the all the charges clearly delineated. Unfortunately we do not have any control over the Priceline website. Had you checked Expedia, or even Booking.com you would see these charges. Typically two rolls of toilet paer are in every room, but we have plenty. You can always call the Front Desk and ask for more.  There is no such thing as Free Parking in this part of the City and our charge is the same as all other Hotels. Coffee, tea, and hot chocolate are available all day long in the Lobby, which reduces the cleanup in each room. Please let me know if you have any other questions or concerns.   Michael

review:
The Best Western Pine Tree Motel is an overall okay option for a short stay, offering a mix of positives and negatives based on my experience. The rooms are quite spacious for the price, and our 2-queen room included a balcony, which was a pleasant feature. However, the heating in the room was inadequate. The window unit provided didn’t heat the space effectively, leaving the room uncomfortably cold, especially during cooler weather.

The motel’s complimentary breakfast was one of its stronger points. While the hot food options were somewhat limited, there was a good variety of choices overall. I particularly appreciated the inclusion of healthier items like probiotic yogurt and better-quality cereal, which added a nice touch to the breakfast experience.

There are a few practical drawbacks to consider. The property does not have gated parking, which might be a concern for some travelers. Additionally, there are no elevators, so carrying luggage to the second floor can be inconvenient. Poor outdoor lighting was another issue that stood out, making some areas feel less safe and welcoming. The bathrooms, while functional, felt outdated with low tubs that could benefit from a renovation.

On a more positive note, the front desk staff were polite and helpful, contributing to a welcoming atmosphere. There is also a small business nook with printing and computer access, which could be useful for guests needing a quick workspace.

Overall, I would recommend this motel for a short stay if you’re looking for an affordable option and don’t mind some of the compromises in comfort and amenities. The spacious rooms, decent breakfast, and courteous staff make it a reasonable choice, but it might not be ideal for longer stays or those seeking a more updated and comfortable experience.

review:
After the derecho that swept through the Midwest in August, 2020, left us without power for four days... and this was on top of the years and years and years of occasional power outages due to thunderstorms in the spring and summer, blizzards in the winter, traffic accidents that took out power poles, and sometimes a transformer exploding after an inquisitive racoon or squirrel got a little TOO curious... we decided we weren't going without electricity again.  The derecho was the last straw.  I did a LOT of research into home-backup generators.  Yes, of course, I looked at the heavily-advertised generator company that starts with a 'G,' but... upon speaking to the professionals at Blackhawk Electric, I chose a Briggs & Stratton model.  I made the commitment to purchase in September of 2020 and, because of COVID-19 affecting supply issues (not to mention the incredible demand for generators -- after the derecho, everyone in the Midwest seemed to have decided on purchasing one for their homes, too), we finally got "the call" yesterday that OUR generator was in and ready to install!  We were ecstatic!  What we paid was money WELL SPENT!  The technicians came out, got everything installed, and cleaned up before leaving.  (Actually, they cleaned MORE than they needed to... stuff that was our mess, not anything having to do with the installation, but these people are true professionals and that's the kind of service you get from people who really care about their work!)  The system is online and I can't wait to be "that guy"... you know, the one who still has lights and air conditioning when everyone for blocks and blocks around is without electricity for days on end!!!

I can't say enough how much I recommend using Blackhawk Electric!  Cindy and Bryan were wonderful to deal with from start to finish, and the three members of the crew who did the installation and testing were all top notch!  Everyone at Blackhawk Electric is prompt, friendly, courteous, and highly detail-oriented!
response_of_owner: Thank you so much.. we appreciate your business and the great review.. we are excited to be finally getting generators in at a fairly regular pace... now that first power outage will be fun to see your neighbors wonder how you have full power lol..

review: I submitted an online request to set up a time for in home estimate. The lady that reached out to me asked me some basic questions like how old and why I was looking to replace the windows. Kind of a slow introduction considering my reason is probably like any other home owner that is in the market. They are old, drafty and not energy efficient. I proceeded to tell her how many total windows my home currently had and that I was looking to replace three main windows at this time. She proceeded to tell me that because of their sale only covers for or more windows that it would be best I go through a Home Depot or Lowe’s. I asked her “so you don’t want to earn my business?” And her response was that it would not be worth my time going through them. Little does she know that my three front windows are over 72 inches wide and the value to replace those windows could essentially be equal to six windows. Needless to say I told her I would take my business elsewhere and it was her loss. Renewal windows by Anderson will never get a good review from me nor will they ever receive my business. So just an FYI for anyone that reads this unless you have four or more windows to be replaced don’t bother calling them. review:
My husband and I booked a birthday weekend getaway to the Public Hotel after years of seeing influencer photos all over Instagram. We’re both super into small space design, so we were pretty excited to experience the unique rooms.

To say we were underwhelmed is an understatement. So many things went awry that I’m worried if I can even fit them all into this review.

First off, for a supposed 4 star hotel, I expect a front desk with multiple staff instead of four iPads in a room with one kinda sour staff member milling around. While checking in, we had to scan our own key cards in order to use them. Once we got to the elevator, we realized one card didn’t end up working, which was frustrating.

We really did appreciate the efficiently designed room, but it felt poorly maintained. The automatic curtains didn’t close all the way, the reading light above the bed was broken, the bed was probably the hardest hotel bed I’ve ever slept on, there wasn’t a duvet cover—just two flat sheets around a duvet, and the bed creaked whenever one of us moved a muscle. Oh, the walls are also paper thin too. We were woken up to our neighbors screaming in the hallway at 4am. Between the hard, creaking bed, the night club music, and the screaming people, I slept horribly.

In terms of amenities, they charge you a nearly $50 fee nightly for basically nothing.  They apparently only have free coffee between the tiny window of 6-8am. There’s very limited toiletries in the rooms. No mini bar. No coffee machine. I think the most comical part of our stay was the “Essentials Closet” across the hall from our room, which contained an ice machine, some gross looking ironing boards, and an empty closet which appeared to at one point in time house -actual essentials- like toilet paper, toiletries, and towels.

It was raining both days of our stay so we took the umbrella in our room with us when we went out. The umbrella completely fell apart within 5 minutes of using it. When we asked for a new umbrella, the person at the front told us they had no more umbrellas. Greeeeaaat.

The common spaces are open to anyone who isn’t staying at the hotel, so I’m not really sure what the point of paying a resort fee is. The second floor was a nice place to hang out, but never in my life have I seen so many sleeping people in a lobby of a hotel. It was unclear if these were even guests. There were huge stains on the couch and also in the elevator after we woke up on Sunday morning. It felt like waking up after overstaying your welcome at a house party.

Everything about this hotel revolves around getting a cool picture for Instagram and not actual comfort or hospitality. It feels more like a college dorm for rich kids than a nice place to stay. It’s all style over substance and it’s clear this hotel is severely understaffed and cutting costs at every turn. I don’t know how they call themselves a 4 star hotel. I would never recommend staying here.
response_of_owner:
Dear Jennifer,

Thank you for taking the time to share your detailed feedback. We’re truly sorry to hear that your experience did not meet expectations. At PUBLIC, we aim to provide a seamless and comfortable stay, and it’s disappointing to hear that we fell short in multiple areas. We appreciate your thoughts on the check-in process and understand that some guests may prefer a more traditional experience. Additionally, we regret that you encountered maintenance issues in your room, including the curtains, lighting, and bed comfort. Our Jefferson beds are designed for optimal rest with a European slat system and premium mattresses, but we understand that preferences vary and would have been happy to provide a mattress topper to better suit your needs. Noise disturbances are something we take seriously, and while we’ve implemented measures to reduce sound transmission, we regret that it impacted your stay.

Regarding the amenities, our All Access Fee covers offerings such as high-speed Wi-Fi, fitness classes, and priority access to our venues, but we recognize that value is subjective and appreciate your perspective. We also regret that the Essentials Closet was not properly stocked and that an umbrella was unavailable when you needed one. This is not the level of service we strive to provide. We take your concerns seriously and will be addressing them internally to ensure a better experience for future guests. While we regret that your stay did not meet expectations, we appreciate your feedback as it helps us continue to improve. If there’s anything further you’d like to discuss, please don’t hesitate to reach out to me at pnguyen@publichotels.com.

Best,

Pierre N
Director of Front Office

You have to request daily housekeeping and they will make a note of it for the time you want to have your room cleaned daily.

There is even a pool and hot tub for those who wish to use it, with dedicated pool towels.  In addition, there is a washer/dryer on the main floor available for those who may need it.

The hotel is situated well if you have a car rental…eg. 15 min drive to Manhattan Beach or the airport. Very close to some great shopping as well. :)

I would not hesitate to book here again…it was excellent value…especially in Los Angeles! Thanks for great service and a wonderful stay! :)

review:
Good location near ballpark, arch, and nightlife. Rooms need upgraded. Can we not have just old baseball themed decor too? Mini fridge needed defrosted, there was a 2" thick sheet of ice along the back of it which made the fridge 50 degrees. Bathroom door would not stay open. They have products in the bathroom but they are very masculine scented. Bed was alright. Pool is closed for construction. They only have 1 working washing machine on site as well. You'll have to go to a laundromat like I did if you are staying a while. Stayed for 2 weeks for a work trip. Parking is 2 blocks away and it is an additional $25 per day for guests, $30 per day for non-guests and $40 per day for event parking. There is valet parking on site at $50 per day. There is a starbucks on site, as well as 2 bars on the main floor, one serving food and the rooftop bar which gets very busy from general public usage. You will get street noise in the room. Housekeeping came every 3-4 days and changed the bedding, emptied trash, and gave fresh towels. Shower pressure sucks. This place needs more elevators than juat 3. Expect to wait in a crowd for elevators between 4-6pm on weekdays due to business trip people returning. They close the first elevator for hotel guests and make it just for the rooftop bar gerneral public guests during busy bar times, and bar goers get priority of the elevators. You can not access floor 26, the rooftop bar on your own with your own room key. You have to go to the lobby to get the elevator attendant to scan a special key.
Food from the lobby bar was pretty good and they played nice rock music in that bar lounge. Rooftop bar's pizza sucked and those servers need appropriate uniforms. Breakfast buffet was really good but was about $22 per person after tax and includes the buffet as well as a made to order omelet and juice. The rooms do not have microwaves and there is a community microwave on each floor but they do not work half the time. I checked 9 floor's microwaves one night juat tryong to heat up some leftover pizza and none of them worked. Had some noisy neighbors for part of the trip. There are always plenty of e-bikes surrounding the hotel. The tv remote in the room was sticky and disgusting. It was an okay stay.
response_of_owner: Hi Kae, we're glad you enjoyed our convenient location and some of the amenities like the breakfast buffet and lobby bar. We apologize for the issues you encountered with the room and facilities during your stay for your work trip. Your comments about the room decor, amenities, and other areas are noted and will be shared with our team for improvement. Please contact us at https://help.hilton.com/s/contactsupport and (314) 421-1776 to discuss further. We appreciate your feedback and hope to welcome you back to Hilton St. Louis at the Ballpark in the future.

review:
We were recommended by a friend who used Prime Moving twice for their moves. We got an in-home estimate for our move and was suggested that we would need five movers for 8-10 hours (3 bedroom house with estimated 70 items and 200 boxes). Shannon was very responsive to all my questions even when I was just in the planning and budgeting phase of the move. I really liked how they have a client site for me to communicate with Shannon and also ensure that my move was scheduled and confirmed.

On the day of my move, the movers and the truck arrived on schedule. One of the guys actually arrived sooner and went straight to work looking over our inventory so he could start planning. Our team of Lucas, Demetrius, Jalin, Arthur, Chris, and Chad were courteous, worked efficiently and only took a break after they were done loading the truck to eat a quick lunch. After eating, they promptly drove over to the new house and started unloading.

In the end, I only needed them for 5 hours but I did a lot of prep work leading up to move day. I moved all of the smaller items and boxes to the new house, broke down all of the furniture (beds, desks, wardrobes), wrapped mattresses, and wrapped pieces in plastic wrap. Prime still covered our pieces with moving blankets before loading onto the truck so many of our belongings made it to the new house without any issues.

Overall, great experience with them, if I ever need to do a local move again, I would definitely use and recommend them.
Tristan was absolutely Amazing, who worked for the valet service! Very quick at retrieving the car and super friendly!

review: 33% doesn't happen because your case is filed with the court, so 40% BEFORE the medical bills, court cost, and your final cut. Don't use 100k to do math because Insurance Companies don't pay out that much unless your Doctor bills are that much. Take your case to trial, don't count on it. Use your own doctors if you want "All" your injuries attended to. Thousands of dollars for copies of Depositions to line the pockets of Deposition companies. Thats your cost because you won't go to trial because that is cost passed onto you. Settlement money's go into NOT your trust and interest earned doesn't go to you.
response_of_owner:
Is this just a complaint about how the personal injury industry works?. 

Everything you described is called a contingency fee that is a contract drafted by the Florida Bar which we all must work under.  The fee is outlined by presuit vs litigation, cost must be reimbursed and doctors need to be paid for their services.  

Personal injury claims are not about getting rich, they are about getting the medical care you need if you are injured, getting your medical bills paid and getting compensated for what happened.

review: Really fishy company. Contractors STAY AWAY! They dont do the work themselves. They hire out but dont stand by their word. I was hired out by them and luckily I did get a down payment but they still owe me $2415.00. My company went out of our way to accommodate FFI / Tera since the job was in Central Illinois and they are out of Fort Meyer Florida. During the process we found out that they had more than adequate time to correct the violations but they dragged on getting the work done. Called several times and then had to contact the city where the project was at. They then revoked the permits on the project and I had the job shut down so that no other contractor can pull a permit for that address. Then went and removed my materials from the house. Called the city 30 days later and they gave me the information of the actual owners which I contacted and they at least apologized and said they were not dealing with FFI on any of their projects anymore and we settled on a fair amount. About 6 months later with the windows busted out and the doors kicked in the city declared it a hazard and I believe it's on the demolition list. Sad for the owners as that property could've made them money had they never dealt with FFI.
response_of_owner: We appreciate the feedback from Mr. Ramos regarding this project from February 2016.  Unfortunately, this industry is not known for its transparency, and what goes on behind the scenes in the decisions of ownership and development companies is largely unknown to subcontractors and service providers alike, including FFI.  What Mr. Ramos may not have realized at the time was that FFI was simply subcontracted as well as GC by the owner - a large conglomerate that buys hundreds of distressed properties and often rents them out in very poor condition - and FFI had their own struggles with this group for both non-payment and uncompensated time dealing with the city on many issues.  The deposit Mr. Ramos received was more than FFI was left with, and FFI did work with service providers who were left with outstanding invoices by paying them outright or working out payment arrangements.  Unfortunately, we do not have a record of Mr. Ramos attempting a workout of his balance.  FFI ultimately ended the relationship with this ownership group around the time of this assignment due to all the issues faced not only at this property but many others.  The ownership group ended up being sued by multiple municipalities for fraud and violations of housing regulations.  We regret that Mr. Ramos had a poor experience with FFI, as our teams strive to consistently excel at treating all clients and subcontractors fairly and with respect.

review:
I am writing my review knowing full well that I'll likely be personally attacked by management, given their responses to prior poor reviews. That's okay, as I'd hope no one else has to have the same experience with this company.

In summary, the company was on time, the crew did a decent job removing the tree (though the more I learn, the more they could have done to avoid lawn damage like using a sheet of plywood to drop limbs onto). However, once the tree was taken down, they let 80% of the tree sit on my lawn over a hot weekend as opposed to hauling the tree away (which they committed to when I agreed to the removal on the same day the tree was taken down). I am over the top about my yard (I work very hard to keep it nice), and I know that about myself - I get that not everyone cares about that. But it's why I cared about confirming the details of the removal process, etc.

I was told the tree was left over the weekend because the removal crew was "done for the week" at 2p on Friday. When raising this concern, Matt (I believe one of the head guys... which is too bad) told me I was inconsiderate and rude, because he was up late the night before working on the trucks and I shouldn't dictate the hours/schedules their crews work. My response was "I have no interest in dictating your schedule, but it sounds like you either need more employees or better trucks, neither of which is your customer's problem to solve. If you don't follow through on your word (removing the tree before the weekend), your customer deals with the consequence."

Matt essentially told me that I needed to give it 2 weeks, and if the grass didn't grow back, we'd revisit the issue - he completely disregarded my concerns and simply made me feel like an idiot. He raked his foot through the dead grass and said "I'm not sure what you're even worried about, this will all come back." So... we waited. After the time passed, it was still completely destroyed. I called him and he said "yeah, I talked to my landscape guy and he basically said what we did probably killed it and burned it all up with the heat." Thanks, Matt - I'm glad your landscape guy could help you understand what your customer tried telling you a few weeks earlier.

Additionally, I confirmed 3 times (once when scheduling the project, and twice during the time the crew was here) that they would NOT lay their grass seed when the project was concluded. Each time, the response I received was "oh, absolutely... you don't want us putting our seed on your lawn - it's just weeds." Well, you guessed it. They did it anyways! I've been fighting weeds in my front yard since - fun!

I would NOT recommend XTreme Tree, especially if you care about the yard that the tree is being removed from. I'd specifically not recommend Matt, who told me multiple times he'd come to replace our sod and make things right. But, weeks later, it still hadn't happened, and I just kept getting texts that said "I haven't forgotten." We got to the end of June (pretty difficult to lay and maintain sod that time of year in Iowa), so I called Matt and said I no longer wanted sod. Instead, I wanted 15% off of my invoice and I'd take care of it on my own. Matt shared that he "could only get comfortable with 10%." I would think good business would be saying "I'm sorry for your experience, we desire to make it right, given we didn't meet the expectation we set."

I contemplated small claims court or just not paying the invoice at all (I was advised by an attorney that this would be a pretty straightforward an easy case to prove), but elected to not do so - this experience had already caused enough time drain. I was told by someone familiar that if that happens, they will come and dump a load of chips in your driveway blocking your in/out ability from your own home. Given our work and daycare obligations each day, I decided it wasn't worth that risk - but talk about a classy way to address your customers! I paid my invoice, and elected to express my frustration through this review, all in hopes of saving someone else the frustration.
response_of_owner:
Hello Elliott - It is with deep regret that we learn of the negative experience you have had with Xtreme Tree. The unhappiness of a large number of customers was never conveyed to the senior management or the owners, which resulted in the reorganization of our office staff. 

The primary inquiry at hand is whether you were content with the tree's removal. Please provide a review regarding the tree removal service that you engaged us for, rather than addressing the issue of grass not growing in the hot Iowa summer weather. Xtreme Tree Team

review:
Last year these guys came out when our septic sensors were going off and said a bulb needed replaced under the electrical box.

They ordered the bulb, which took weeks and it was not the right size. Finally, after going back and forth with the "owner" (I don't know if he actually was the owner or just a manager that took the calls) they got the right bulb and came out to install. Unfortunately, we found out this month when our sensors started alarming again, they installed it incorrectly, not removing the plastic from the bulb and also damaging the electrical fuse box above it.

When we called them out to look at it, instead of taking any sort of accountability, they had the gull to try and sell us an entirety new $22k system. According to my texts, the technician's name is Aaron. They couldn't fix the box and didn't have a replacement bulb either, said they would have to order it.

We called another company for a second opinion and they came out a day later, with the replacement bulb, telling us the electrical box was an easy fix that they could take care of for a few hundred dollars.

I understand this company has a good reputation for installing new systems and maybe some of their other services, but unfortunately they just don't have deep knowledge of "older" septic systems and simple problem solving. We're lucky their mistakes didn't cause more damage.

The last thing I will say is: your technicians need some manners. Bad talking other companies they know nothing about and very making ignorant claims about how you have no idea how to fix someone's issue isn't how you get business.
response_of_owner:
Cheyenne,
Sorry to hear there was clearly some communication issues. We had already ordered a replacement bulb to replace the existing bulb because one of our previous employees had possibly installed it improperly.  The damage to your fuse box was there last year and electrical contact was repaired to try to save you money instead of replacing entire unit, per your request. This is all clearly documented last year as well. As for giving you your husband the information on approximate cost of a new system is because he asked for the information and no one was trying to sell anything. If one of our employees was saying anything about another company that will be addressed immediately as I definitely don’t agree or stand for that. We wish you you the best.

review:
We contracted with Patti Sanders at Earth Works to install pavers on our driveway and paths in late March 2021. Over the next month we looked at their extensive collection of pavers at their location and visited with several customers.
We finally decided on a color and pattern about a month later and ordered the pavers knowing that it would take several months to get on their schedule. Then came Covid and the paver manufacturers closed down and the installers had to be furloughed.
August 2nd the pavers and installers arrived. Chris Cooprider was the foreman with his buddy, Matt. Very Great guys!.
First was demolition. The "Locate"  people never came (they locate underground pipes and  wires) so the AT&T internet wire was broken. AT&T was very responsive and we had service in one day but when they buried the wire they nicked the water main. JEA was also very responsive so neither issue was a problem. After demolition, soil was removed to a depth of 6 inches. Chris and Matt then ran several pipes under the driveway so in the future wires could be pulled without disturbing the pavers. They also ran a drain from a downspout to the street . Then came tamping and 6 inches of "crushcrete" which is like a coarse porous sand that is the base for the pavers. Under Chris' direction a team of guys came to lay the pavers. They worked incredibly fast and precisely, even in the August heat. On the second day of paving they did the detail work: cutting pavers to fit,   and installing edging, and curbing that was placed over concrete. A special synthetic sand was vibrated and swept between the paver blocks and hardened by watering in. The final day (8/11) Chris and Matt did the clean up, set sprinklers, put down sod, notched the edge of the pavers that indicted where the underground pipes were placed, power washed the front of the house, and washed and cleaned the shrubbery. The place looks great!
In 30-40 days, after the pavers weather, another team will return to clean and seal the pavers.
All in all we are very pleased with the job and particularly Chris and Matt for their guidance, expertise and professionalism.
